title: inference-experiment-telemetry-checklist-and-trace-hypotheses
content:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic checklist and set of tracing/metric hypotheses for ad-hoc inference experiments and model variant rollouts. Meant to be used by engineering on-call, SREs enabling experiments, and ML engineers instrumenting canaries. This is intentionally terse — copy into experiment docs or a ticket as needed.

Audience:
- ML engineers running model A/B or quantization experiments
- SRE/Observability for alerting & dashboarding
- Product/Eng owners for SLO verification

High-level goals (what we need to learn from telemetry):
- Is new model/quantization affecting tail latency (p95/p99) or increasing variance?
- Are tokens being emitted slower during warmup or steady-state (per-token latency)?
- Does routing to different hardware (e.g., a100->h100 quantized) create hotspot/backpressure?
- Can we detect silent correctness regressions via surrogate signals (prompt-step token drop, re-renders, increase in assistant-turn length)?
- What's the cost delta per 1M tokens for the variant in production traffic mix?

Metric definitions (canonical names & labels we will use):
- inference.request.count (labels: model, model_version, customer_tier, route, region, env) — increment per request.
- inference.request.success (labels same) — boolean success counter (200-equivalent).
- inference.request.error (labels: error_type, http_status, model, model_version) — counter.
- inference.latency.ms (histogram) — end-to-end request latency including queueing, in ms. Buckets should emphasize [1,5,10,25,50,100,250,500,1000,2000,5000]ms.
- inference.token.latency.ms (histogram) — per-emitted-token latency from runtime token generation step. Very useful to detect kv-cache or attention perf regressions.
- inference.kv.cache.hits / inference.kv.cache.misses — counters if prefix caching used. Labels: model, model_version, cache_key_hint (if available).
- inference.queue.depth (gauge) — number of requests waiting to be executed on a pool. Labels: pool_id, region, hw_type.
- inference.gpu.utilization.percent (gauge) — by worker node. Labels: node_id, hw_type.
- inference.cost.tokens (derived) — computed in analytics, but emit approximation per request if inexpensive (labels: model, quantization).
- inference.prompt.truncated.count — counter when prompts are truncated due to length limits (labels: model).

Tracing/span design (recommended minimal spans + tags):
- Root span: request_id, route, model, model_version, customer_id (if permitted), env, region.
- Spans: auth, routing/lookup, queue/wait, scheduling, allocator.assign, model.load (cold-start), inference.engine.forward (per-layer aggregate optional), tokenization.encode, tokenization.decode, streaming/send-chunk, postprocess/cleanup.
- Important tags/attributes: batch_size, seq_len_input, seq_len_output, kv_cache_used (bool), quantized (bool), hw_type, kernel_variant, weights_loaded_from_disk (bool), cold_start (bool).
- Span IDs: keep deterministic naming for easy search (e.g., inference.engine.forward -> inference.forward).

Sampling rules & trace retention (pragmatic):
- Policy: 100% sampling for errors. For non-error traffic: 5% baseline + 20% for canary/model_version=staging. For high-QPS customers with reserved capacity, sample 0.5% to conserve bandwidth.
- Retain full traces for 14 days for canary tags and errors; aggregated traces (event counts only) retained for 90 days.
- When debugging performance regressions, flip sampling to 100% for affected pool_id for a short window (use toggle in Console).

Dashboard wireframe & notes (what to build quickly for an experiment):
Top row (single-glance health):
- Request rate (timeseries) split by model_version (stacked area)
- 95/99 latency heatmap (model_version vs region) — bucket-based heatmap of latency distribution
- Error rate (rolling 5m) and top error types (bar)
- Cost estimate rate (approx cost per minute based on tokens)

Middle row (dive by path):
- Queue depth + avg queue wait per pool (timeseries)
- GPU utilization by node (small multiples)
- Token-latency histogram and p50/p90/p99 lines
- KV-cache hit ratio trend (if used)

Bottom row (traces & incidents):
- Recent high-latency traces (link to trace viewer) with quick filter for model_version=canary
- Canary test results (synthetic prompts) pass/fail rate + example outputs (link to artifact storage)
- Correlation view: requests with long token.latency.ms and high GPU io/wait

Alerting sketch (start conservative, iterate):
- P99 latency > X ms for 5m for any production model_version -> Sev2. X should be set per model class (small/medium/large).
- Error rate > 0.5% over 10m and > baseline by 3x -> Sev1 for hosted customers; Sev2 for internal experiments.
- Queue depth > threshold (pool-specific) for > 2m -> investigate autoscaler or routing.
- Synthetic canary failure (>=2 consecutive failures) -> Pager and stop rollout.
- Cost spike alert: tokens-per-minute * cost-per-token > budgeted_rate * 1.5 -> oncall notify finance+product.

Experiment instrumentation checklist (copy into PR/MR):
- [ ] Emit model_version label everywhere (routing, runtime, traces)
- [ ] Add canary=true label for experiment traffic (and route tag)
- [ ] Ensure token.latency.ms is exported from the runtime (per-token timing, not averaged)
- [ ] Add sampling override flag for the experiment in trace pipeline
- [ ] Add synthetic runner config (prompts, expected assertions) and wire results to dashboard
- [ ] Compute cost delta stub (per-request approximate tokens * cost model) and emit as metric or log line
- [ ] Add note in release notes and link to experiment dashboard

Cost telemetry: what to correlate
- tokens emitted vs p99 latency: are long outputs also more expensive? (obvious but sometimes hidden)
- batch sizes vs per-token latency: larger batching may reduce cost but increase tail latency for small requests — look for trade-offs.
- hardware type vs token throughput (A100 vs H100 vs CPU quantized): include kernel_variant label to separate heatmaps.

Trace+Metric debugging heuristics (operational playbook snippets):
- If p99 spikes and GPU utilization is low: suspect serialization/queuing or distributed lock. Check queue.wait span and scheduling spans.
- If p99 spikes and GPU util ~100%: either kernel ineff or increased seq_len — inspect token.latency by seq_len bucket.
- If per-token latency rises but end-to-end latency stable: check tokenization/streaming spikes (tokenization.encode / streaming/send-chunk spans).
- If errors increase and no corresponding code change: check model weights (version mismatch), disk IO for weights, or RPC timeouts to model-serving workers.

Open questions / TODO (action items):
- Decide canonical bucket boundaries for token.latency.ms (we currently have inconsistent buckets across services). ACTION: define and push to metric library (owner: Luis).
- Should we emit per-layer timing for the top 3 models for deeper perf analysis? Pros: rapid root-cause for attention vs matmul; Cons: high cardinality. Proposal: sample 1% of canary traces with per-layer aggregates only. (owner: Olivia)
- How to safely log customer_id for traces without violating PII rules? Need SRE + legal guidance and a hashed customer id approach. (owner: Ben)
- Correlate infra events (preemptions, node reboots) with inference incidents automatically. Need to join infra logs in analytics pipeline. (owner: eng-infra)

Notes to self / quick heuristics (informal):
- If experimenting with extreme quantization, first look at token.confidence (if we can create a proxy) or abrupt increases in prompt.truncated.count — these sometimes show hallucination/regression signs before user feedback.
- Keep synthetic prompt set small but diverse: 30 prompts with short/long contexts + a heavy-token-output prompt. Run every 5m for canaries.
- For canary rollouts, route 1% of traffic for 30m with 100% trace sampling, then inspect token.latency and error signals before increasing to 5%.

Slack/links snippets to include in experiment tickets: 
- "Observability checklist applied: token.latency exported, canary label, 100% trace sampling enabled for canary. Dashboards: inference-experiment (top) and canary-synthetic-runner (bottom)."
- Attach link to trace snippet: [Trace viewer link placeholder]

Appendix: quick field glossary (one-line):
- token.latency.ms: time (ms) to generate a single token inside the model forward path (exclude network/serialization).
- queue.wait.ms: wall time spent waiting for scheduler to assign GPU.
- kernel_variant: runtime-chosen kernel implementation tag (e.g., f32-default, int8-fused-attn).
- cold_start: boolean flag for requests that triggered model load.

End — keep iterating. If you copy this into Confluence, please strip the checklist to just the boxes and add owners/duedates.
